scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four adults and a child in modest robes sit or stand beneath a grapevine beside a stone house, looking attentively toward the upper left. Clay jars and pink flowers frame the courtyard, and a winding road leads toward sunlit hill towns under a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listening townspeople and road between towns imagine the setting of Jesus' teaching and preaching after He finished instructing the Twelve. Jesus remains outside the frame. The particular listeners, courtyard and landscape are artistic choices, not details supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a brown robe sits behind an iron prison gate, raising an open hand toward two robed men. Warm daylight falls across stone walls, an earthen jar and a folded woven mat; a sunlit passage appears at right.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined visit represents John hearing of Christ's works and commissioning his disciples. Their faces, gestures, clothing and prison details are artistic choices. Two disciples form an illustrative group; the supplied Greek says 'through his disciples' and does not specify their number. Christ's works are conveyed as news rather than pictured. Jesus remains outside the scene.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in long robes stand in a sunlit stone courtyard under an olive tree. The man in a rust-colored mantle holds one hand to his chest and extends the other palm upward toward the right. His companion stands behind with clasped hands; blue hills and village roofs appear beyond a low wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined questioner and companion embody the question addressed to Jesus: is He the Coming One, or should they expect another? Their open gesture and attentive faces convey an appeal awaiting a reply. Jesus remains outside the frame. The courtyard, clothing and exact arrangement are imaginative details, not claims supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in cream tunics and rust and olive mantles look attentively left. One carries a leather satchel. Pale stone houses, grape leaves, olive trees and a flower-lined path fill the sunlit watercolor village landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Their attentive gazes and the open path imaginatively connect hearing and seeing with the instruction to go and report to John. Jesus remains outside the picture. The two figures, courtyard, clothing and landscape are illustrative choices, not details specified by this verse; no particular miracle is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man steps through a sunlit stone courtyard beside a resting wooden crutch. An older seated man opens his hands, while three plainly dressed listeners look toward the right; one woman holds a hand near her ear. Olive branches, distant hills and clay jars frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering selects restored sight and walking, hearing, and the poor receiving good news from the verse's list. The crutch and listening gesture are visual cues, not details supplied by the text. Jesus remains outside the frame. The cleansing of lepers and raising of the dead are affirmed in the explanation but are not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a cream headcloth and terracotta robe seated beneath an olive tree. His hands rest on his knees and his sandaled feet are planted beside a stony path. He gazes upward to the right, with wildflowers, golden hills and distant stone houses around him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined listener receives the words of Jesus, who remains outside the frame, with quiet attention and trust. His settled posture and securely planted feet gently echo not stumbling. The verse concerns not taking offense at Jesus or falling away because of Him; the path is a visual analogy, not a claim that Jesus is a physical obstacle or that this scene is a recorded event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of robed listeners looking attentively to the right beside tall, wind-bent reeds and a rocky stream. Two travelers walk away along a winding path through dry golden hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The wind-bent reeds picture Jesus' rhetorical question, while attentive listeners and two departing travelers echo the verse. Jesus and John are not depicted. The stream and arrangement are imaginative; the verse does not place this speech beside these reeds or describe John as wavering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in long burgundy and blue robes converse beneath sunlit stone arches. Cushions and fringed fabric cover a bench beside pottery and a gold-colored vessel; flowering vines, a mosaic floor and distant dry hills complete the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined royal household illustrates Jesus' example of people wearing soft garments in kings' houses. The anonymous figures, fine robes and sheltered arcade make that contrast tangible; the verse does not describe this particular conversation or palace. Jesus is outside the scene.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a coarse brown robe stands on a rock beside a stream, raising an open hand toward attentive, modestly robed listeners. Wildflowers line the stony path beneath a leafy tree and warm, distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined wilderness gathering recalls the people going out to see John the Baptist, whom Jesus affirms to be a prophet and more than a prophet. The listeners' attention connects the scene to that question. The river, clothing, poses and flowers are illustrative choices beyond the details stated in this verse. Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a coarse brown garment over a cream tunic walks along a sunlit, winding stone path, extending one hand toward the way ahead. An olive tree, rocks and small wildflowers frame golden hills beneath a pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The lone messenger represents John going ahead to prepare the way for Jesus, who remains outside the picture. The open wilderness path gives imaginative visible form to his preparatory ministry; the verse does not describe literal road construction. His clothing, gesture and landscape are illustrative details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a rough brown mantle stands beside a river with open hands, while a man in a patched robe walks beneath a flower-covered stone arch toward a sunlit garden. Olive branches, reeds, distant hills and small wildflowers surround the path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative meditation, not a recorded meeting: the honored John stands by the river, while an anonymous humble person approaching the radiant garden represents even the least in the kingdom. The open arch and continuous path suggest the kingdom's greater standing without depicting John as rejected. The garden is an artistic metaphor, not a description of heaven; greatness is not physical size.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of three robed men bracing against a partly opened wooden gate in a sunlit limestone arch. One pushes the planks, another presses behind him, and a third grips the door edge. Through the gap are a stone path, flowers and an olive tree; a hillside village lies beyond the wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The pressured doorway is an imaginative metaphor for the verse's violence and grasping, not a recorded siege or a literal entrance to heaven. The men straining at the wood echo the supplied passive reading, 'is taken by violence.' Quiet light beyond suggests the kingdom's preciousness without portraying God or Jesus. The image does not teach that violence earns entry.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a large open blank parchment scroll and several rolled scrolls on a wooden table beneath a rocky overhang. Beyond them, a bearded man in a shaggy brown cloak raises one hand beside a reed-lined river, with flowers, olive branches and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The scrolls imaginatively represent the Law and the collective witness of the prophets; their arrangement leads the eye toward John beside the river, recalling that they prophesied until John. This symbolic juxtaposition is not a recorded meeting or an event described in the verse. Jesus is outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a coarse brown outer garment stands beside a river, extending one hand toward a seated man and woman in modest robes. Reeds, rocks, leafy branches and sunlit hills surround them in a warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined riverside scene represents John the Baptist's prophetic ministry; the listeners' open hands evoke willingness to receive Jesus' teaching. Matthew 11:14 identifies John as the promised Elijah who was to come. The setting and gestures are artistic additions, not events stated in this verse; no meeting with Elijah or depiction of Jesus is intended.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle sits beneath an olive tree, cupping a hand behind one ear and looking up to the right. Wildflowers, a sunlit path, olive groves, distant hills and pale village buildings surround him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The attentive listener illustrates the verse's call to hear. His cupped hand and receptive expression make listening visible. The hillside, clothing and individual are imaginative setting details, not an event or person named in this verse. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five children in long robes sit facing one another on stone steps in a sunlit marketplace. A child cups a hand beside an open mouth while another reaches toward the opposite pair. Fruit baskets, clay jars, cloth awnings and flowering vines surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The seated children calling across the marketplace give visible form to Jesus' comparison. Their faces, clothing and market surroundings are imaginative details, not a claim that this was a recorded event. The scene stays with this verse without adding the games described afterward.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Draft illustration intended for Matthew 11:17: Village children play flutes in a market square while others stand still with folded arms, a small drum and a flute on the ground, cloth awnings overhead.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Placeholder illustration. This imaginative study aid has not been reviewed for visual or historical accuracy.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a rough brown cloak stands empty-handed on a sunny stone path. Behind him, three robed villagers whisper and point from a shaded doorway. Bread and a clay cup rest untouched on a stone ledge beside flowers and an olive tree, with hills and village houses beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village-edge encounter represents John's abstinent life through his empty hands and untouched bread and cup. The villagers' whispering and pointing stand for the accusation that he has a demon. No demon is depicted, because the verse reports their accusation rather than affirming it. The location, people and meal arrangement are illustrative, not details supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men smile as bread is passed across a courtyard table set with flatbread, olives, clay cups and a pitcher. A coin pouch and a few coins rest at the left. Two frowning men confer in the shaded doorway behind them, beneath warm stone walls and olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard meal evokes fellowship with tax collectors and sinners; the coin pouch hints at that social setting. Jesus remains outside the picture. The disapproving onlookers recall the accusations against Him, while shared bread and welcome suggest wisdom recognized by her deeds. The verse does not identify this particular meal or these guests.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a sunlit stone town. A bearded man stands with folded arms, another walks away down the lane, and a veiled woman turns toward a doorway. A rolled woven mat rests on a step beneath leafy branches; olive trees and distant hillside houses fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Galilean street uses turned backs, averted faces and folded arms to suggest the cities' refusal to repent. The rolled mat is an artistic reminder of past works of mercy, not a detail supplied by the verse. Jesus' rebuke is represented indirectly; He is outside the frame. No particular miracle or subsequent judgment is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Coarse brown sackcloth hangs over a low stone seat beside a clay bowl of gray ashes. Olive branches and pottery frame a sunlit arch overlooking blue harbor water, wooden boats and pale coastal houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life uses sackcloth and ashes to evoke the repentance Jesus says Tyre and Sidon would have shown. The coastal setting recalls those cities without claiming an exact location or an event that occurred. The verse's woe against Chorazin and Bethsaida remains a warning about their response to His mighty works.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bronze balance on a limestone ledge above a blue sea. Two small coastal town models and a few stones occupy the higher left pan; one town model and larger stones fill the lower right pan. An olive branch rests beside the base under a softly clouded sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This is an imaginative visual analogy, not an event described in the verse. The two coastal town models in the raised pan stand for Tyre and Sidon; the single town and heavier stones in the lowered pan stand for the hearers' greater judgment. Both pans carry stones, preserving the comparison of severity rather than suggesting exemption. The balance and models are artistic devices; God and Jesus are not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A sunlit stone town beside a blue lake rises behind a ruined gateway. Worn steps curve down into a deep, dark rocky cleft. Olive trees, dry golden grasses, scattered carved stones and distant purple hills surround the scene beneath a cloud-filled sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The downward stair and dark cleft symbolize Capernaum's threatened descent to Hades; the ruined stones recall Sodom, which Jesus says would have remained had it received the same mighty works. This is an imaginative comparison, not literal geography or a claim that Capernaum was destroyed in this manner. Jesus and particular miracles are left unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bronze balance stands on a stone slab in a warm, rocky landscape. Its raised left pan holds ruined buildings; its lower right pan holds an intact miniature stone town. A winding path, trees, distant hills and violet clouds surround it.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The balance and miniature towns are an imaginative comparison, not objects or an event described in the verse. The raised ruined settlement evokes Sodom; the lower, heavier intact town evokes the place Jesus warns. The unequal pans express more tolerable versus more severe judgment, without suggesting that Sodom escapes judgment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two young children in cream and terracotta robes sit on a woven mat, smiling upward attentively. Behind them, two robed men study a blank scroll beneath an olive tree. The sunlit stone courtyard overlooks golden hills and a village beneath a blue sky with soft clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative courtyard contrasts the children's receptive wonder in sunlight with learned adults studying in shade, reflecting the Father's revealing and hiding in Jesus' praise. The verse does not narrate this gathering or identify these things as the scroll. Jesus stays outside the frame; the Father is not depicted. Sky and earth recall His lordship over both. The contrast does not condemn learning.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two open hands in cream linen sleeves face upward above a rocky hillside path. An old olive tree, wildflowers and low stone walls frame distant hills and a small village beneath a warm blue-and-gold sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The praying hands imaginatively suggest Jesus' willing yes to the Father's good pleasure while keeping Him otherwise out of view. The quiet hillside supports reverent assent; neither this setting nor the gesture is specified by the verse. The natural sky does not depict the Father.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed listeners sit beside a stone archway as a hand draws back a golden curtain, revealing a sunlit garden with an olive tree, red and yellow flowers, and a winding path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined doorway scene illustrates disclosure, not an event reported in the verse. The unseen curtain-drawer's hand suggests the Son revealing the Father to those He chooses. The garden and sunlight evoke received understanding; they do not depict the Father or express the whole mystery of the Father and Son's mutual knowledge.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Under sunlit olive trees, an older man in ochre and a woman in green rest beside a rope-tied bundle and woven basket. Both look upward to the right. A third traveler approaches carrying a load; pale hills and a distant village lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: These imagined travelers and their lowered loads illustrate the weary and burdened whom Jesus invites to Himself. Their shared gaze suggests His invitation beyond the frame; He is not depicted. Physical loads visualize weariness and the promise of rest without claiming that the verse recounts this particular scene or limits His rest to relief from manual labor.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A wooden yoke with two curved bows rests on sunlit limestone beneath an olive tree. An empty stone bench and terracotta jug stand nearby, while a winding path leads through fields toward distant hills and a village.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Galilean resting place uses the intact yoke to picture accepting Jesus' teaching, while the shaded seat and peaceful path suggest His promised rest for souls. The verse does not describe this location or these objects as a historical scene. Jesus is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A honey-brown wooden double yoke and a woven basket holding cream linen rest on a pale stone bench. Olive branches shade a sunlit courtyard, with wildflowers, a clay jar, a winding path, cultivated fields and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The intact yoke and modest basket imaginatively pair the verse's two images. Their peaceful setting evokes the ease and lightness Jesus describes. The courtyard is an illustrative composition, not an event recorded in the verse; no figure represents Jesus.
